;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[2020 Democratic Republic of the Congo massacres]]
***[[Allied Democratic Forces]] militants attack a village in [[Ituri]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], killing 35 people. It is the second attack in the town in two days. The [[terrorist]]s assaulted civilians with knives and firearms and destroyed the village. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200911-suspected-militia-fighters-kill-dozens-in-dr-congo-s-eastern-ituri-province (France24)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Three people are killed and seven others injured after an [[al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] [[suicide bomber]] blew himself up at a restaurant in [[Mogadishu]], [[Somalia]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/09/dead-suicide-bomber-targets-mogadishu-restaurant-200909162810348.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Four [[Malian soldier]]s are killed in an attack in [[Alatona]], by suspected [[Islamist]] militants. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2020/09/11/news/world/at-a-glance-world/4-killed-in-mali-attack/766990/ (''Manila Times'')]
*[[Second Saudi–Yemeni War]]
**The [[Houthis]] say that they attacked an "important target" in [[Saudi Arabia]]'s capital, [[Riyadh]], using a [[ballistic missile]] and [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]]s. A spokesman for the movement confirmed the attack without explaining, while there was no comment from the Saudi side. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-saudi/yemen-houthis-say-they-attacked-important-target-in-riyadh-with-missile-drones-idUSKBN2611PF?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**A [[United States dollar|$]]300 billion stimulus bill proposed by the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] is blocked in a 52–47 vote in the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/senate-voting-gop-covid-19-relief-proposal/story?id=72926403 (ABC News)]
*The [[pound sterling]] weakens after the [[European Union]] says the ongoing [[trade negotiation between the UK and the EU]] would be "put at risk" if the [[United Kingdom]] failed to "withdraw or amend" its [[UK Internal Market Bill|Internal Market Bill]] before the end of this month. The UK replies that it has "the right to overrule parts" of the [[Brexit withdrawal agreement]]. [https://sports.yahoo.com/brexit-eu-uk-internal-market-bill-withdrawal-agreement-pound-euro-dollar-150356069.html (Yahoo!)]
*[[Rio Tinto (corporation)|Rio Tinto]] CEO [[Jean-Sébastien Jacques]] and two other senior executives resign amid an enquiry into the destruction of the 46,000 year old [[Hamersley Range|Juukan Gorge]] caves in [[Western Australia]], which is considered an [[Australian Aboriginal sacred site|Aboriginal sacred site]]. Rio Tinto destroyed the ancient rock shelters while expanding the [[Brockman 4 mine]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2020/sep/11/rio-tinto-ceo-senior-executives-resign-juukan-gorge-debacle-caves?CMP=Share_iOSApp_Other (''The Guardian'')] 

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 California wildfires]]
**The death toll in the [[North Complex Fire]] in [[Northern California]] rises to ten, while 16 people are missing, according to the [[Butte County Sheriff's Department]]. [https://eu.rgj.com/story/news/2020/09/10/north-complex-fire-update-map-butte-county-california-wildfire-deaths/5767037002/ (''Reno Gazette Journal'')]
**The town of [[Berry Creek, California|Berry Creek]] in [[Butte County, California|Butte County]] is reported as being "mostly destroyed". [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/wildfires-california-oregon-washington-death-toll/ (CBS News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports its single largest increase in a day, recording 95,735 new infections. The Health Ministry also reported 1,172 deaths in the past 24 hours. The ministry says the increase is due to a surge in testing as experts warn that the virus is spreading to towns and villages. [https://apnews.com/906e35ca3d2852f5da98bebacb4811ff (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports 3,861 new cases in the last 24 hours, taking the nationwide total to 207,203. This is a single-day record high since the pandemic began in the country. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5167578/pecah-rekor-lagi-tambah-3861-kasus-positif-corona-di-ri-jadi-207203 (''detikNews'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[Minister of Health (France)|French health authorities]] report 9,843 new cases in France over the past 24 hours, setting a new record high for the country since the beginning of the pandemic. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/amp/world-europe-54111209 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports 372 new cases in the last 24 hours, its highest daily tally since the start of the pandemic in the country. From those new cases, 114 were due to an outbreak at a food processing plant in northern Greece, with 133 recorded in the greater [[Athens]] area. [https://mobile.reuters.com/article/amp/idUSKBN2612XI (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Guatemala]]
***[[Guatemala]] is expected to reopen their [[Borders of Guatemala|borders]] after closing them for six months in an effort to stop the spread of COVID-19. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/guatemala-reopen-borders-week-months-72928593 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania#Kiribati|COVID-19 pandemic in Kiribati]]
***[[Kiribati]] announces it will keep its borders closed until the end of the year to keep the country free of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. The presidential office announces some exceptions, including repatriation flights, with 20 I-Kiribati arriving soon from the [[Marshall Islands]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/425703/kiribati-borders-remain-closed-for-2020 (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[AstraZeneca]] [[CEO]] [[Pascal Soriot]] says that the vaccine results could be ready by the end of the year if trials resume. Clinical trials were temporarily suspended after a participant in the trials began to develop symptoms associated with [[transverse myelitis]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-astrazeneca/astrazeneca-expects-covid-vaccine-result-by-year-end-if-trials-resume-idUSKBN2611C2 (Reuters)]
***[[Sinopharm]] began Phase III trials in [[Peru]] starting with two dozen people, with the goal to vaccinate 6,000 people between the ages of 18 and 75. So far, Sinopharm has given 30,000 doses to volunteers and another 10,000 participants have received double doses in [[Bahrain]] and the [[United Arab Emirates]], with additional trials planned for [[Morocco]] and [[Argentina]]. [https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/third-phase-human-trials-coronavirus-vaccine-underway-peru (VOA)]

;International relations
*[[French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] and [[German Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] agree to accept into their respective borders around 400 [[unaccompanied minor]]s from the [[Mytilene#Moria|Mória Reception & Identification Centre]] on the [[Greek island]] of [[Lesbos]]. It was Europe's largest [[refugee camp]], destroyed by fire the previous day. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-09-10/merkel-macron-open-doors-to-400-minors-from-greek-refugee-camp (Bloomberg)]

;Law and crime
*[[Dominican Republic tar scandal]]
**The [[Attorney General of the Republic (Dominican Republic)|Dominican Republic Attorney General]] receives the first case on the former [[Public works|Minister of Public Works]] and [[2020 Dominican Republic general election|presidential candidate]] of the [[Dominican Liberation Party]] (PLD), [[Gonzalo Castillo (politician)|Gonzalo Castillo]], in the purchase of hot [[tar]] for [[Dominican peso|RD]]$11.5 billion ([[United States dollar|US]]$194.9 million). [https://dominicantoday.com/dr/uncategorized/2020/09/10/dominican-republic-us194-9m-hot-tar-scandal-heads-toward-indictment/ (Dominican Today)]
*[[2019–2020 Colombian protests]]
**Seven people are killed and 248 others injured during protests against [[police brutality]] in [[Colombia]], which are sparked after the death of a man who was pinned to the ground and repeatedly [[taser]]ed by [[National Police of Colombia|police]] in [[Bogotá]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-54078852 (BBC News)]
*Former [[Prime Minister of Vanuatu]] [[Charlot Salwai]] is set to stand trial from November 23, charged with ten counts of [[bribery]] and [[corruption]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/425746/former-vanuatu-pm-to-stand-trial-in-november (RNZ)]
